proof:
Source: parent proof, the claim (CL*) with V3 (reduction to cycles, including the n = 1 segment construction), V4(o) and V4(i), the "Application" paragraph of V4, and the last sentence of V15. The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) are the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems (not available to this child, hence assumed) cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem, dtc_vanish_off_support; CL(d), BR(d) are the closure and boundary-rectifiability statements in degree d. Siblings used: cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq (restrict_unique), cbr_measure_convergence_tools ((MM)), cbr_isoperimetric_filling (isoperimetric), cbr_slice_property_of_weak_limit (slice_limit), cbr_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity (cycle_im). n := d + 1, M := mass in ℝ^P, ‖ω‖_∞ := sup|ω(x)|, ISP the integer slice property of the statements of slice_limit and cycle_im.

0. Preliminaries. (i) For an admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X in ℝ^P and a Borel set E, X⌞E(ω) := ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ is a current (linear; |X⌞E(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞μ(tsupport ω), so test-form-convergent sequences are mapped to convergent sequences) with M_W(X⌞E) ≤ μ(W ∩ E). (ii) The zero current is IM (empty IMRep), and by (IMC)(c) differences of IM currents are IM; hence A + B := A − (0 − B) and all integer combinations of IM currents are IM. (iii) |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖_∞; masses are subadditive.
1. Basic properties of T. If tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅ then T_j(ω) = 0 by (VO) (spt T_j ⊆ K), so T(ω) = 0: spt T ⊆ K. By lower semicontinuity (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf, WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), M(T) ≤ liminf M(T_j) < ∞ and M(∂T) ≤ liminf M(∂T_j) < ∞, and ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T; likewise spt ∂T ⊆ K.
2. ∂T is IM. Apply CL(d) in U := ℝ^P to the IM currents ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T: for every open W, M_W(∂T_j) ≤ sup_j M(∂T_j) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn(∂T_j, W) = 0 (by definition if d = 0; if d ≥ 1 it is M_W(∂∂T_j) = M_W(0) = 0).
3. A compactly supported IM filling Y of ∂T (V3). Case n ≥ 2 (d ≥ 1): Z := ∂T is IM with compact support (spt ∂T ⊆ K closed), ∂Z = ∂∂T = 0 and M(Z) < ∞; isoperimetric with m := d − 1 gives an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = ∂T, M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y inside a bounded thickening of spt ∂T, so spt Y (closed) is compact. Case n = 1 (d = 0): ∂T is an IM 0-current with compact support. Let (M₀, θ, ξ) be an IMRep; H⁰ is the counting measure, so θ ≥ 1 on M₀ and, by (MR), M_G(∂T) = Σ_{x∈M₀∩G}θ(x) for open G; by (VO) this vanishes for open G disjoint from spt ∂T, so M₀ ⊆ spt ∂T ⊆ K, and M₀ is finite (local integrability on the compact set spt ∂T). As in degree 0 the orientation is ±⟨·⟩ (⟨α⟩ := α(∅)) at every point, so ∂T(g) = Σ_{i=1}^N m_i⟨g(x_i)⟩ with x_i ∈ K and m_i ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}. Choose ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K; then ∂T(ζ) = T(dζ) = lim_j T_j(dζ) = 0 by (VO) (dζ = 0 near K ⊇ spt T_j), so Σ_im_i = 0. Fix x₀ ∉ {x_1, …, x_N}. Segment currents: for x ≠ x₀ let τ := (x − x₀)/|x − x₀|, I := {x₀ + s(x − x₀) : 0 < s < 1} (open segment) and [[x₀, x]](ω) := ∫_I ω(τ) dH¹. It is IM: carrier I (Borel; countably 1-rectifiable as a subset of the range of the Lipschitz map ℝ → ℝ^P, u ↦ x₀ + uτ), mult := 1 on I, orient := (β ↦ β(τ)) (a unit orientation of the line ℝτ: (τ) is orthonormal and spans it); at every y ∈ I, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 I y (ℝτ), because blowUpMap y r maps I onto the segment {uτ : −|y − x₀|/r < u < |x − y|/r}, which contains (ℝτ) ∩ tsupport f for small r (f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P)), so ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' I} f dH¹ = ∫_{ℝτ} f dH¹ for small r; H¹(I) = |x − x₀| < ∞. H¹⌞I is the push-forward of Lebesgue measure on (0, |x − x₀|) under the isometric parametrization u ↦ x₀ + uτ, hence ∂[[x₀, x]](g) = ∫_0^{|x−x₀|} dg(x₀ + uτ)(τ) du = ∫_0^{|x−x₀|} (d/du)⟨g(x₀ + uτ)⟩ du = ⟨g(x)⟩ − ⟨g(x₀)⟩. Let Y := Σ_i m_i[[x₀, x_i]], IM by 0(ii); ∂Y(g) = Σ_im_i(⟨g(x_i)⟩ − ⟨g(x₀)⟩) = Σ_im_i⟨g(x_i)⟩ = ∂T(g); spt Y is contained in the convex hull of {x₀, x_1, …, x_N} (compact); M(Y) ≤ Σ_i|m_i||x_i − x₀| < ∞.
4. The cycle Γ := T − Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P): ∂Γ = ∂T − ∂Y = 0; spt Γ ⊆ spt T ∪ spt Y is a closed subset of a compact set, hence compact; M(Γ) ≤ M(T) + M(Y) < ∞.
5. ISP of IM currents (V4(i)). Claim: if X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and ∂X are IM and both have locally finite mass, then X has ISP. Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of X, ∂X and f L-Lipschitz. (SL) with these data gives currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', and Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t with M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for open W. For k, m ∈ ℕ, (MM) (constant sequence, G := B_k(0), (a, b) := (−m, m), μ(B_k(0)) < ∞) gives M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞ for a.e. t ∈ (−m, m); so for a.e. t, Z_t has locally finite mass. Fix such t. Let R_X = (M_X, θ_X, ζ_X) be an IMRep of X; (IMC)(b) with E := {f < t} gives an IM current A' represented by (M_X ∩ {f < t}, θ_X, ζ_X); restrict_unique (U := ℝ^P; the admissible representations (μ, ξ) and (R_X.measure, ζ_X) of X — admissible by (IMC)(d) — and (0, 0)) gives A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ζ_X(ω) dR_X.measure = A'(ω), so A_t is IM. In the same way B_t is IM (IMRep of ∂X). ∂A_t = B_t + Z_t has locally finite mass (M_W(B_t) ≤ μ'(W)), so ∂A_t is IM by BR(d) in U := ℝ^P. By (IMC)(c), Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t is IM. Any A, B satisfying the defining formulas equal A_t, B_t (currents are determined by their values), so ∂A − B is IM for a.e. t: X has ISP.
6. Application. Each T_j has ISP by step 5 (T_j and ∂T_j IM with finite mass); Y has ISP by step 5 (Y IM, ∂Y = ∂T IM, finite masses). slice_limit (CL(d), (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL); sup_j(M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) ≤ sup_j(M(T_j) + M(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every W; T_j ⇀ T) shows that T has ISP.
7. Γ has ISP (V4(o)). Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of Γ, ∂Γ and f L-Lipschitz. Let (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), (μ_Y, ξ_Y), (μ_{∂Y}, ξ_{∂Y}) be (REP) representations (finite masses). ISP of T and of Y, instantiated with these, gives a null set N such that for t ∉ N the slices Z^T_t := ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t} and Z^Y_t := ∂(Y⌞{f<t}) − (∂Y)⌞{f<t} (restriction currents of 0(i) w.r.t. these representations) are IM. Let t ∉ N and A, B with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ'. Since T = Γ + Y on every test form, restrict_unique with (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ, ξ), (μ_Y, ξ_Y) and E := {f < t} gives T⌞{f<t} = A + Y⌞{f<t}; likewise ∂T = ∂Γ + ∂Y gives (∂T)⌞{f<t} = B + (∂Y)⌞{f<t}. Hence ∂A − B = Z^T_t − Z^Y_t, which is IM by (IMC)(c). So Γ has ISP.
8. Conclusion. By cycle_im (CL(d), (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO); ∂Γ = 0, M(Γ) < ∞, spt Γ compact, ISP), Γ is IM. Since T = Γ − (0 − Y) as currents, T is IM by (IMC)(c) (0 is IM). ∎
key_steps: spt T ⊆ K, finite masses; ∂T is IM by CL(d).
Fill ∂T by a compactly supported IM Y: isoperimetric if d ≥ 1, signed segments from a point if d = 0 (total multiplicity 0 by (VO)).
Γ := T − Y is a compactly supported cycle of finite mass.
IM currents with IM boundaries have ISP ((SL), (MM), (IMC)(b),(c), restrict_unique, BR(d)); hence T_j, Y have ISP and T has ISP by slice_limit.
Linearity of restrictions (restrict_unique) gives ISP for Γ.
cycle_im makes Γ IM; T = Γ − (0 − Y) is IM by (IMC)(c).
